VTS Scoring Log

Core Peptides

US-facing gray market· Lyophilized vials· Scored July 2026· corepeptides.com →

Core Peptides is the longest-running vendor in the current catalog - 7+ years in operation with over 100 SKUs - and scores lowest on documentation among established operations. The site claims independent verification but names no lab, publishes no COA database, and provides no lot codes. The gap between operational scale and verifiable documentation is what drives the Low score: it is not that testing is absent, but that none of the claimed testing is independently confirmable from public materials.

28 /100
Low Transparency
A long-running operation with a large catalog and third-party testing claims, but verification is structurally blocked: no public COA database, no named lab, no batch-level traceability accessible to buyers before or after purchase. Documentation discipline lags considerably behind the "independently verified" marketing claim.

Community Signal
Independent Test Results
No community-commissioned independent test results identified in public forums as of July 2026. Community testing coverage for Core Peptides is limited relative to their catalog size and operational history.
Community Experience
Core Peptides appears in vendor discussion threads as a budget-accessible option with a broad catalog. Community references are largely neutral on quality specifics; the operation's longevity is the primary positive signal cited.
Scoring Notes
The gap between claim and evidence
Core Peptides' primary transparency problem is not that they test poorly - it's that they provide no public mechanism to verify that they test at all. "Independently verified" is a claim. A named lab, a batch-specific COA, or a public test results page is evidence. The gap between those two things is the score.
What would change the score
Adding a dedicated lab testing page naming the lab and method, publishing batch-specific COAs searchable by lot number, and expanding the refund policy to include lot-quality incidents would move this score substantially. The operational track record and catalog size are genuine strengths the testing infrastructure currently undermines.
